summary: Ubisoft Shanghai's post-apocalyptic survival game, now maintained through GOG's Preservation Program.

entries.title: I Am Alive
entries.definitive_edition: GOG Preservation Program build 1.01 or later

emulation.notes: Use the native GOG Windows build. Console emulation is unnecessary and provides no sourced content advantage.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Native PC resolution and high-refresh output with GOG's modern-system fixes.

primary.version: GOG Preservation Program build 1.01 or later
primary.why: GOG's maintained build is DRM-free and directly fixes modern-Windows launching, input-device stutter, high-refresh displays, controller support, and hardware validation. It is now the cleanest and highest-fidelity way to play the same campaign.
primary.how_to_play: Install the current GOG build, record its changelog version, use a controller to avoid the original mouse-camera stutter path, and keep the intended monochrome/film-grain treatment unless making a documented comparison.

all_releases.reason: skip: historically first, but lower settings and resolution than the restored PC build.
skip: no sourced exclusive campaign content and a lower technical ceiling than PC.

all_releases.fidelity: Original native-PC release with widescreen and higher-resolution output.
all_releases.reason: skip: superseded by the maintained GOG build, which fixes several modern-system and input problems.
skip: convenient for existing owners, but still the console build.

all_releases.fidelity: Maintained DRM-free PC build with modern OS, input, controller, high-refresh, and stutter fixes.
all_releases.reason: primary: best current compatibility and capture route without changing the campaign.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: No sourced platform-exclusive story content requires a console pass; the maintained GOG build resolves the practical PC compatibility disadvantage.

entries.remaster_caveats: This is a preservation update, not a visual remaster. The black-and-white image, depth of field, and film grain are part of the original presentation; disabling them changes the art direction.
